description: SURPRISE IS THE PROMOTION MECHANISM. A channel is not a candidate for authority until the model is surprised about it — either a reading contradicts its expectation (detected) or the forward model projects it to a crossing before contact (predicted). Surprise mints a candidate carrying its axes separately; the existing collapse decides. No standing per-effector weight, no scalar, and no rule that knows what a fall, a desk or a wall is. The resolution chain (measured -> expected -> declared) is a precondition rather than hygiene: a dark channel cannot surprise you, so it can never promote and its effector can never be rescued. v1.1.0 BUILDS THE STREAM route (b) needs: a channel's own observation history, scoped to the current trial, is read as a sequence and projected forward to a crossing, so the predicted route is reachable instead of merely present. It also replaces three declared literals with the graph data they were ratios to — the channel's measurement quantum, the ledger's control horizon, and the ledger's own reach as the floor an unpriced option must lose to.

rules.name: srp_resolve_channel_from_measurement
rules.comment: A published observation is the strongest rung. Provenance says so, so nothing downstream can mistake it for an assumption.

rules.name: srp_resolve_channel_from_expectation
rules.comment: WE EXPECT TO TURN, WE ASSUME WE HAVE. With no observation the efference copy's prediction stands in — usable, and flagged as an assumption rather than a reading.

rules.name: srp_resolve_channel_from_declared_prior
rules.comment: Neither read nor predicted: the declared prior, explicitly marked. This is the rung that replaces the silent zero — a channel with no information says so instead of reporting 0 like a measurement.

rules.name: srp_expect_channel_from_enacted_program
rules.comment: An efference copy is not a measurement and not a policy: it is what the issued command already said would happen. A channel with no declared predictor mints nothing and stays unsurprisable, which is an honest statement about the body rather than a gap.

rules.name: srp_expect_vertical_channel_from_enacted_program
rules.comment: An efference copy is not a measurement and not a policy: it is what the issued command already said would happen. A channel with no declared predictor mints nothing and stays unsurprisable, which is an honest statement about the body rather than a gap.

rules.name: srp_detect_surprise_from_violated_expectation
rules.comment: Surprise is the reading against the expectation, over the channel's own declared tolerance. Both sides must exist: a channel with no expectation cannot be surprised, and neither can a dark one.

rules.name: srp_scope_channel_stream_to_current_trial
rules.comment: The channel's stream epoch is the latest trial its observations carry. UNCONDITIONAL, because `MaxOver` over `Neighbours` is an aggregate and aggregates read as their identity inside a `where` while being correct in an effect — measured, not assumed. It does not need a guard: it is a pure function of the observation set, so re-firing rewrites the same number.

rules.name: srp_read_channel_history_as_a_stream
rules.comment: Until this rule existed nothing in the graph turned a channel's observations into a sequence, so no projection could be attached and route (b) was unreachable — the predicted route was present in the rule set and dead in every run. UNCONDITIONAL for the same reason as the scope rule above: the aggregates must live in an effect. Note the RAW `value_units` read: a sample carrying no reading must poison the stream into no-fit, never coalesce to 0, because 0 is exactly the origin the crossing is measured to and a missing reading would otherwise report maximum urgency.

rules.name: srp_project_channel_stream_to_a_crossing
rules.comment: The missing half of route (b). `crossing` at the MEASURED order is margin/rate generalised: an accelerating approach reports sooner than the linear reading, and the difference is the curvature the linear reading throws away. `horizon_units` is recorded ON the projection because `crossing` returns the bound BOTH when the stream crosses at it and when it never crosses at all; the consumer needs to tell a deadline from the absence of one.

rules.name: srp_refresh_channel_projection_from_the_current_stream
rules.comment: Unconditional over the projections this seed minted, so the crossing is always the reading of the stream as it stands rather than the reading it had when the projection was first attached. A pure function of the stream, so re-firing rewrites the same numbers and the fixpoint terminates.

rules.name: srp_predict_surprise_from_projected_crossing
rules.comment: ANTICIPATION, NOT REACTION. A projected crossing inside the declared horizon promotes with NO contact having occurred. This is the route that lets a falling body reach for the ground before it arrives, and nothing here knows what falling is.

rules.name: srp_promote_surprised_channel_to_candidate
rules.comment: The whole of authority allocation. An effector no goal is using becomes contestable the moment something about it is surprising — which is why nothing is ever zero and why no standing weight is needed. The axes are carried SEPARATELY into the collapse; this rule invents no scalar and picks no winner.

rules.name: srp_mark_candidate_affordable_against_ledger
rules.comment: Whether the collapse MAY take a candidate is separate from whether it wants to. Reachable = min(stock, rate x horizon) already keeps the amount and rate ceilings apart; a candidate costing more than is reachable is marked unaffordable and stays visible, so the refusal is legible rather than silent.

rules.name: srp_adopt_simulator_effector_into_episode
rules.comment: An attached simulator publishes effectors under its connection. The episode adopts them so the ledger and the frontier can reach them. The adapter never writes this edge itself.

rules.name: srp_open_authority_pareto_profile
rules.comment: One frontier per episode, declaring how many objectives it compares. `dimension_count` is the number of axes, not a weighting of them.

rules.name: srp_publish_candidate_to_authority_frontier
rules.comment: The promotion layer's whole output: a candidate with its axes carried SEPARATELY onto the frontier the rest of cognition already uses. `cp_recognize_relational_dominance` does the comparing; this seed never picks a winner. Cost is the only negated axis, because it is the only one where more is worse.
